How much flood risk is here?

FEMA's National Risk Index rates New Hanover County's coastal flood risk Relatively High and inland flood risk Relatively Moderate, from expected annual loss.

  • Coastal flood riskRelatively High
  • Coastal modeled annual loss (county)$6,688,939/yr (Relatively High, 86th national percentile)
  • Inland flood riskRelatively Moderate
  • Inland modeled annual loss (county)$46,006,218/yr (Relatively Moderate, 43rd national percentile)

Modeled annual loss is FEMA's estimate for the whole county (all buildings), not any one home's expected loss or premium, and not a flood probability.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective NRI 2023 release; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

Am I required to carry it?

About 64.6% of the NFIP policy units in this dataset for New Hanover County are in mapped high-risk (A/V) zones — not 64.6% of all buildings. In a Special Flood Hazard Area a federally backed mortgage legally requires flood insurance.

  • Zone AE9,771 policy units
  • Zone X6,231 policy units
  • Zone VE1,584 policy units
  • Zone A1049 policy units
  • Zone B18 policy units
  • Zone C7 policy units
  • Zone A096 policy units
  • Zone V131 policy units

Zone mix by policy units (summed policyCount). Federal rule: a lender must require flood insurance on a building in a Special Flood Hazard Area with a federally backed loan (42 U.S.C. §4012a). This is the mix of existing policies, not of all buildings, and does not establish any one property's obligation.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective July 31, 2026; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

How much does it cost here?

Among existing single-family primary-residence NFIP policies in New Hanover County, the median annual cost is $963, with the middle half between $683 and $1,224 (8,754 policies). This is what current policyholders pay — a new policy on a different building can differ.

Each policy's annual cost (premium plus fees), single-family primary residences. The bar is the middle half (p25–p75); the orange line is FEMA's full-risk price.

Coverage in force: $4,010,917,000 of building and $995,183,000 of contents coverage across all New Hanover County policies.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective July 31, 2026; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

Can I pay less than the sticker price?

4 of New Hanover County's 5 NFIP communities carry a Community Rating System discount that cuts every eligible policy's premium — up to 20% inside the high-risk zone (Carolina Beach, Town Of).

CommunityCRS classHigh-risk discountOther-area discount
Carolina Beach, Town Of620%10%
New Hanover County715%5%
Wrightsville Beach, Town Of715%5%
Kure Beach, Town Of810%5%
Wilmington, City Of—No discountNo discount

The Community Rating System cuts NFIP premiums for every eligible policy in a community that does extra flood work. The discount shown is the community's rate; what share of its policies currently receive it is not in this data. Confirm with your agent.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective October 22, 2026; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

What do floods actually pay out here?

Between 1978 and 2026, New Hanover County had 11,183 paid NFIP flood claims totalling $187,170,979.

Orange bars are the three costliest years: 1996 ($86,406,774), 2018 ($34,340,522), 1999 ($30,804,440). Net building + contents payments by year of loss. Claims are matched by the claims dataset's county code, which may not exactly match a policy's property county.

That is 11,183 paid claims since 1978 against 17,667 policies in force today — a cumulative tally spanning ~49 years over a present-day snapshot, not an annual claim rate or a flood probability.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective 1978–2026; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

How common is flood insurance here?

New Hanover County has about 15.1 NFIP flood policies for every 100 homes (17,667 policy units vs 117,236 housing units).

  • NFIP policy units17,667
  • Housing units117,236
  • Policies per 100 homes15.1

A coverage-commonness proxy: policy units include some multi-unit and non-residential policies and exclude private flood insurance, so read it as how widespread NFIP coverage is here, not an exact share of households.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA NFIP + U.S. Census ACS 5-year 2023 (B25001), retrieved October 22, 2026.

How often is this county a flood disaster?

New Hanover County has had 22 distinct federal flood, hurricane or tropical-storm disaster declarations. The most recent:

  • 2024 — Tropical Storm: Potential Tropical Cyclone Eight
  • 2024 — Tropical Storm: Hurricane Helene
  • 2024 — Tropical Storm: Tropical Storm Debby
  • 2022 — Hurricane: Hurricane Ian
  • 2020 — Hurricane: Hurricane Isaias
  • 2019 — Hurricane: Hurricane Dorian

Distinct storms by calendar year (one storm's emergency and major-disaster declarations are counted once), not individual declaration records.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective declarations through 2026; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

More data: FEMA disaster aid & reconciliation

Did the government pay homeowners after floods?

FEMA approved $6,841,472 in Individual & Households housing help to New Hanover County homeowners across 5 disasters, on 11,735 valid registrations.

FEMA Individual Assistance is disaster aid, usually capped and partial — separate from NFIP insurance and not a substitute for a policy.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective owner registrations by disaster; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

Reconciliation & data completeness

Our counts are checked against FEMA's official figure and the API's own totals.

In-force count: 17,667 policy units (from 13,706 API records; condo-association records carry more than one unit). FEMA official reconciliation count pending for this county. Count reconciliation (not a snapshot proof): policies: 13706/13706 fetched; claims: 11183/11183 fetched.

What this data cannot tell you

  • Your own premium — it depends on elevation, coverage and deductible. We show where existing policies fall.
  • Private (non-NFIP) flood insurance prices.
  • Your address's exact flood zone — use FEMA's Flood Map Service Center.
  • Why premiums are rising — we show the gap to full-risk, not the cause.
  • A year-over-year premium trend — the in-force snapshot holds only current-term policies, so a like-for-like multi-year index isn't possible from this data. A per-effective-year median is shown only where several years of policies exist.
